policy: Primary research and official professional guidance inform bounded runtime behaviors; no source is treated as proof that an LLM provides therapy or guaranteed personal change.

sources.citation: Ryan, R. M., & Deci, E. L. (2000). Self-determination theory and the facilitation of intrinsic motivation, social development, and well-being.
sources.runtime_use: Preserve choice; explore autonomy, competence, and relatedness as optional lenses rather than universal diagnoses.
sources.limitation: Broad theory and review, not a validation of AI coaching or a complete account of motivation.

sources.citation: Motivational Interviewing Network of Trainers. Understanding Motivational Interviewing.
sources.runtime_use: Use partnership, reflective listening, open questions, summaries, permission before advice, and an engage-focus-evoke-plan rhythm.
sources.limitation: Professional guidance, not an efficacy trial; this skill borrows non-clinical conversational behaviors and does not claim to deliver MI.

sources.citation: SAMHSA TIP 35: Enhancing Motivation for Change in Substance Use Disorder Treatment (2019 update).
sources.runtime_use: Avoid confrontation and unsolicited direction; elicit the user's reasons and plans when ambivalence is central.
sources.limitation: Clinical substance-use guidance; only general communication principles transfer, not assessment or treatment procedures.

sources.citation: Theeboom, T., Beersma, B., & van Vianen, A. E. M. (2014). Does coaching work?
sources.runtime_use: Treat coaching as potentially useful for outcomes such as goal-directed self-regulation, while keeping claims modest.
sources.limitation: Organizational human coaching studies; does not establish equivalence for an LLM copilot or every personal-growth domain.

sources.citation: Grassmann, C., Scholmerich, F., & Schermuly, C. C. (2020). The relationship between working alliance and client outcomes in coaching.
sources.runtime_use: Agree on goal and task, invite corrections, and periodically check whether the conversation remains useful.
sources.limitation: Correlational association across human coaching processes; relationship quality may partly reflect other factors and should not be anthropomorphized.

sources.citation: Locke, E. A., & Latham, G. P. (2002). Building a practically useful theory of goal setting and task motivation.
sources.runtime_use: Make chosen goals clear and observable while checking commitment, difficulty, feedback, and task complexity.
sources.limitation: Much evidence concerns performance settings; specificity can be counterproductive for exploration, learning, or poorly understood tasks.

sources.citation: Gollwitzer, P. M., & Sheeran, P. (2006). Implementation intentions and goal achievement.
sources.runtime_use: When intention is strong but initiation is weak, offer a user-chosen if-then cue and response.
sources.limitation: Effects vary by domain and depend on an active underlying goal; a plan does not solve missing resources, skills, safety, or commitment.

sources.citation: Wang, G., Wang, Y., & Gai, X. (2021). A meta-analysis of the effects of mental contrasting with implementation intentions on goal attainment.
sources.runtime_use: Optionally contrast a desired outcome with the most relevant present obstacle, then form an if-then plan.
sources.limitation: Small-to-moderate pooled effect with publication-bias concerns and limited moderator evidence; never present as a guaranteed formula.

sources.citation: Harkin, B., et al. (2016). Does monitoring goal progress promote goal attainment?
sources.runtime_use: Agree on a small observable measure and review point when monitoring will inform adjustment.
sources.limitation: Monitoring can burden or distort behavior; use only with consent and do not turn it into surveillance or self-worth scoring.

sources.citation: Michie, S., et al. (2013). The behavior change technique taxonomy v1.
sources.runtime_use: Name active ingredients precisely, such as goal setting, action planning, prompts, feedback, or social support.
sources.limitation: A classification system, not evidence that every technique works for every user or context.

sources.citation: Lally, P., van Jaarsveld, C. H. M., Potts, H. W. W., & Wardle, J. (2010). How are habits formed: Modelling habit formation in the real world.
sources.runtime_use: Use stable context cues, allow variable formation time, and treat a missed repetition as data rather than failure.
sources.limitation: Small observational sample and selected daily behaviors; no universal day count should be promised.

sources.citation: Tannenbaum, S. I., & Cerasoli, C. P. (2013). Do team and individual debriefs enhance performance?
sources.runtime_use: Use brief structured reviews of intended versus actual events, causes, learning, and next adjustment.
sources.limitation: Mostly training and work performance contexts; a growth review must not imitate critical-incident psychotherapy.

sources.citation: MacBeth, A., & Gumley, A. (2012). Exploring compassion: A meta-analysis of the association between self-compassion and psychopathology.
sources.runtime_use: Use non-shaming recovery language after setbacks and separate a missed action from global self-judgment.
sources.limitation: Primarily correlational association with psychopathology; does not prove that generic reassurance causes better goal attainment.

sources.citation: American Psychological Association. Health advisory: Use of generative AI chatbots and wellness applications for mental health (2025).
sources.runtime_use: State the difference from qualified care, minimize sensitive data, avoid unvalidated mental-health claims, and route needs beyond scope.
sources.limitation: Advisory guidance rather than a controlled study; local laws and platform requirements may add obligations.

sources.citation: Fang, C. M., et al. (2025). How AI and human behaviors shape psychosocial effects of chatbot use.
sources.runtime_use: Avoid high-engagement and exclusivity tactics; encourage real-world action, human connection, and stopping points.
sources.limitation: Preprint, four-week study, and general chatbot use rather than this skill; dependence findings require cautious interpretation.

sources.citation: Between Help and Harm: An Evaluation Study of Mental Health Crisis Handling by Large Language Models (2026).
sources.runtime_use: Treat crisis handling as a dedicated safety path and keep behavioral crisis cases in the release suite.
sources.limitation: Benchmark performance changes with model versions and does not turn a general LLM into an emergency service.
